 Toyota Crown Signia GT-S Concept Reimagines the SUV as a Sleek Wagon 
 A lowered stance and a handful of tweaks transform the humble Crown Signia into the GT it’s always dreamed of being.
 By Andrew Wendler Published: Oct 28, 2026 Save Toyota Conceived and assembled by the Toyota Motorsports Garage, the Crown Signia GT-S concept features a nearly five-inch lower ride height and custom 21-inch wheels. 
 A custom front air dam, aggressive rear aero, and some cosmetic enhancements on the flanks add to the aggressive posture. 
 Interior mods are subtle, including red accents and heavily bolstered seats. 
 We already dig the Toyota Crown Signia ’s understated style because its profile leans more towards the station wagon aesthetic instead of the generic SUV style most players in its segment aspire to. Even so, there’s a bit too much daylight between its tires and wheel wells for our tastes, and it just seems to be crying out—maybe “whimpering” is a better word—for a little extra flair on its flanks.
 Apparently, the folks at Toyota Motorsports Garage picked up on our thoughts via ESP, because how else would one explain the Toyota Crown Signia GT-S Concept they built for SEMA 2026?

 Toyota Featuring a nearly five-inch lower ride height(!), the suspension utilizes custom one-off coil-over dampers from MCS (Motion Control Suspension), while rolling stock comes courtesy of HRE (born from Howald Racing Enterprises) in the form of 21-inch wheels wrapped in 295-mm (11.6-inch) Toyo tires. To improve stopping, Toyota pinched the calipers from an RX500h F Sport, tweaking them slightly before mounting them at all four corners.
 The drop alone is enough to transform the Crown Siggy, but Toyota wanted to ramp up the visuals too, making sure to cover the larger tire and wheel combo with widebody fenders and then covering it all in a custom-mixed dark gray hue accented by bonus flake and numerous coats of clear. Then it massaged the front headlamp covers and rear fascias, highlighting their work with touches of red outline that extend to the rest of the vehicle, including the logos and rear-view mirrors.
 Toyota Toyota The interior gets a lighter touch, gaining heavily bolstered seats with red piping and headrests emblazoned with embroidered GT-S lettering. A similar treatment adorns the shifter.
 Finally, Toyota addressed the aero situation with what it calls a “sporty aero package.” While that may be true, Toyota is underselling those undulating vents carved into each front fender, the front air dam, and the cosplay rear diffuser. They all look the part; whether they improve performance or not remains to be seen.
 Toyota Toyota Toyota didn’t mention any specific powertrain tweaks aside from the custom dual exhaust pipes that are integrated into the rear bodywork. Still, we’d love to see some of these bits make it to consumers via Toyota’s TRD or TGR factory aftermarket programs.
